acquisitions.title: AWS Weekly Roundup: Welcome DuckLabs to the team, Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD), and more (August 31, 2026)
acquisitions.excerpt: Amazon Web Services has signed a definitive agreement to acquire the Amsterdam-based company DuckLabs, which is known for developing the open-source analytical database DuckDB. DuckDB will remain open source under its independent foundation and the MIT license following the acquisition. Co-founded by Hannes Mühleisen and Mark Raasveldt, DuckDB runs locally or directly on Amazon S3 and executes SQL against files such as Parquet, CSV, and JSON. The database is designed for everyday queries of a terabyte or less and pairs effectively with AI agents. Over time, AWS plans to integrate DuckDB's query speed with enterprise-scale services including Amazon Redshift, Amazon Athena, Amazon S3, Amazon EMR, AWS Glue, and Amazon SageMaker. Mühleisen and Raasveldt will continue to lead the technical direction of the project. Additionally, Vice President and Distinguished Engineer Andy Warfield discussed the acquisition and analytics trends in a post titled DuckDB and the changing physics of analytics on the All Things Distributed blog.

launches.title: Accelerating the borderless Lakehouse: Announcing preview of cross-cloud caching
launches.excerpt: Google Cloud has announced the preview of cross-cloud caching and cross-cloud connections for its borderless Lakehouse architecture, designed to improve multi-cloud analytics and artificial intelligence workloads. The new features enable enterprises to query governed data directly where it resides across platforms such as Amazon S3, Azure Data Lake Storage, and Google Cloud Storage. By federating catalogs through the Apache Iceberg REST specification, the system connects to external platforms like Databricks Unity Catalog, AWS Glue, and Snowflake Horizon. The newly introduced cross-cloud caching feature transparently accelerates queries in BigQuery while reducing remote network transfer costs. The caching mechanism operates at a sub-file block granularity for columnar formats like Apache Parquet, ensuring that only specific column chunks and dictionary pages are fetched and stored locally. Cached data blocks feature default encryption at rest using Google-managed encryption keys, while cache entries remain strictly partitioned by project and catalog boundaries to ensure regional data residency compliance. To maintain data accuracy, BigQuery checks remote object metadata before utilizing cached information, allowing upstream table modifications to prompt the retrieval of new files. Furthermore, the preview of BigQuery cross-cloud connections allows organizations to connect BigQuery directly to raw standalone files in Amazon S3 and Azure Storage without requiring an Iceberg catalog. Together, these enhancements aim to lower the total cost of ownership for cross-cloud data processing by significantly reducing the volume of data that must be transferred across the wire.

launches.title: Kimi K3 by Moonshot AI is now generally available on Amazon Bedrock
launches.excerpt: Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 model is now generally available on Amazon Bedrock, expanding the platform's open weight model portfolio. According to Moonshot AI, Kimi K3 is its most capable model to date and the first open model to reach 2.8 trillion parameters. The model combines native vision capabilities with a one-million-token context window, making it suitable for tasks such as long-running coding sessions across large repositories, multi-document analysis, and extended agent workflows. Moonshot AI reports that Kimi K3 achieves an approximate 2.5 times improvement in scaling efficiency compared to the previous Kimi K2 version. On Amazon Bedrock, the model operates within the same security boundary as proprietary models and utilises consistent controls for access, encryption, and auditing. Furthermore, Kimi K3 is the first open weight model on Amazon Bedrock to support explicit prompt caching, which helps reduce both latency and input costs when context is reused across multiple model calls. The model is currently accessible in all AWS regions where Amazon Bedrock is available by utilising cross-region inferencing. Users can begin using the service through the Amazon Bedrock Console, while additional information is available in the official documentation and the launch blog post.

launches.title: The new AgentCore Runtime is now available in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
launches.excerpt: Amazon Web Services has announced the availability of the next generation of AgentCore Runtime, which is the serverless microVM compute within Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. The updated runtime introduces elastic memory management designed to reclaim unused memory throughout a session, ensuring that users pay for actual usage instead of peak consumption. This approach allows each session to begin with a small memory profile, while additional memory is allocated on demand as workloads require it. Furthermore, the architecture eliminates the need for pre-provisioning, supports scaling to zero, and provides hardware-enforced session isolation. To improve performance, the new runtime prepares the agent environment once and creates a snapshot, allowing every new instance to restore from that snapshot instead of repeating the full startup sequence. This mechanism maintains consistent cold start times regardless of container image size or concurrency levels. In testing, the updated runtime achieved a P75 cold start time of 1.9 to 2.0 seconds for container images ranging from 200 megabytes to 2 gigabytes, whereas the previous version took between 5.4 and 30 seconds. The next-generation runtime is currently available in five specific regions, namely US East (N. Virginia), US East (Ohio), US West (Oregon), Europe (Ireland), and Asia Pacific (Tokyo). Users can begin utilising the updated compute environment by setting the platform version to V2 when creating or updating a runtime.

launches.title: AWS PrivateLink announces Tunnel Endpoints to access network segments
launches.excerpt: Amazon Web Services has introduced tunnel endpoints for AWS PrivateLink, allowing customers to privately and securely access entire network segments in another virtual private cloud or account. Previously, customers who wished to share resources with external parties had to create individual resource configurations for every single resource one at a time. With the new functionality, users can instead create a single resource configuration representing an entire Classless Inter-Domain Routing range within their network. This configuration can then be shared with external vendors using AWS Resource Access Manager. Once shared, the vendor is able to create a new type of virtual private cloud endpoint known as a tunnel endpoint. Vendors utilise GENEVE encapsulation to tunnel through this endpoint into the customer's virtual private cloud, granting them access to the resources contained within the specified range. Pricing for the new feature includes an hourly charge for maintaining the tunnel endpoint alongside a per-gigabyte fee for any data processed through it. The capability is currently available across a wide range of global AWS regions, including multiple locations in the Americas, Africa, Asia-Pacific, and Europe. Further information and guidance on getting started with the feature can be found directly within the official AWS PrivateLink documentation and pricing pages.

launches.title: New low-cost burstable Amazon EC2 T8i instances are generally available
launches.excerpt: Amazon Web Services has announced the general availability of new low-cost burstable Amazon EC2 T8i instances powered by custom sixth-generation Intel Xeon Scalable Processors. These instances are designed to deliver up to thirty percent better price performance compared to previous generation T3 instances. They target low-to-moderate CPU utilisation workloads such as microservices, development and testing environments, low-traffic websites, and data processing jobs. Similar to T3 instances, the new T8i models utilise a CPU credit system that provides a baseline level of performance with the ability to burst above it when required. Unlimited mode serves as the default credit configuration for these instances, which are offered in nano, micro, small, and medium sizes. The hardware supports distinct vCPU-to-memory ratios of 1 to 0.25, 1 to 0.5, and 1 to 1. Customers can purchase the new instances via On-Demand and Spot instances, with Savings Plan options expected soon, while smaller micro and small variants are also accessible under the AWS Free Tier. T8i instances support shared tenancy exclusively and are currently available across multiple AWS regions in North America, the Asia-Pacific region, and Europe.

geo.title: German Chancellor Merz vows to stay on despite 'disaster' in state election
geo.excerpt: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has vowed to remain in office despite exit polls indicating severe defeats for his centre-right Christian Democratic Union party in two state elections held on Sunday. In the north-eastern state of Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, the far-right Alternative for Germany party was projected to win the most votes, while the CDU was expected to only narrowly enter parliament, prompting Merz to describe the outcome as a disaster. Meanwhile, in Berlin, the ruling CDU was projected to finish behind Die Linke. These results follow a major victory for the AfD in Saxony-Anhalt a fortnight prior, compounding mounting pressure on Merz amid poor approval ratings and speculation regarding a potential mid-term replacement. Despite the pressure, Merz stated that he would press ahead with his coalition government's planned economic, tax and welfare reforms, describing them as essential for the country. Public broadcaster ZDF projected the AfD to secure 38 percent of the vote in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, ahead of the SPD on 36 percent, though the AfD is not expected to govern due to a refusal by other parties to cooperate. In Berlin, the CDU was projected to achieve 20 percent of the vote, trailing Die Linke at nearly 26 percent. Although eight German state leaders expressed backing for Merz earlier in the week, he faces deep unpopularity and criticism that his shift to the right on immigration has alienated voters while failing to diminish AfD support.

geo.title: Germany's Merz vows to press ahead with reforms after historic state election defeat
geo.excerpt: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has announced his intention to remain in office following severe electoral defeats for his party in two state elections. Exit polls published by public broadcaster ARD showed the center-right Christian Democratic Union securing just five percent of the vote in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, marking the party's lowest state result since the Second World War. In Berlin, the CDU was projected to finish second with twenty percent, trailing behind the Left party at twenty-four point five percent. Merz acknowledged the outcome as a disaster but struck a defiant tone, rejecting any retreat from the government's reform agenda for Europe's largest economy. He argued that the country's economic and political challenges made difficult and potentially unpopular reforms even more urgent, pledging to press ahead with steadfastness. The anti-migration and Russia-friendly Alternative for Germany party made significant gains during the voting. Merz has faced a damaged authority following a previous defeat to the AfD in Saxony-Anhalt, a result that stunned observers and could lead to the formation of the nation's first far-right regional government since the war. Having become leader sixteen months ago to revive a stagnant economy, the seventy-year-old chancellor has grown deeply unpopular amidst a sullen national mood. Despite facing calls from within his own party to step down over the past two weeks, top-level allies have warned against personnel debates. In anticipation of a difficult political period, Merz cancelled a planned trip to New York for the United Nations General Assembly and reaffirmed his determination to finish his term.

geo.title: Trump says triumphal arch will be military complex with drones and snipers
geo.excerpt: US President Donald Trump has announced that his proposed triumphal arch project will double as a military complex capable of storing equipment and deploying snipers and drones. Writing on his Truth Social platform on Sunday morning, Trump stated that the plans were being updated for national security purposes at the strong request of the US military. The facility will be designed to house large numbers of drones and snipers on the roof and plaza areas, alongside large quantities of sniper ammunition in storage. He did not provide specific details regarding construction plans or timelines, and it remains unclear whether the facility requires further approval. Trump noted that Washington DC is allegedly the only one among fifty-nine top global cities and capitals without a triumphal arch. Construction on the 250-foot structure, planned for a site across the Potomac River from Washington DC near Arlington National Cemetery, was expected to begin this month. Earlier architectural renderings feature a golden Lady Liberty flanked by two gold eagles, with patriotic phrases inscribed on either side. At 250 feet, the arch would be taller than the nearby Lincoln Memorial and half the height of the Washington Monument. The Department of Defence declined to comment further when contacted. This project is one of several construction initiatives pursued by Trump during his second term to revamp the US capital, alongside a White House ballroom and various other renovations.

invest.title: My rental property is paid off, but I need cash. Is this a bad time to take out a $50,000 HELOC?
invest.excerpt: The Federal Reserve announced a quarter-percentage-point interest-rate hike on Wednesday, raising the federal funds rate to a range of 3.75 percent to 4.0 percent. The decision comes as central banks continue efforts to address ongoing economic pressures and inflation through tighter monetary policy. Borrowers considering financial products such as home equity lines of credit will likely see the cost of variable-rate loans increase following this adjustment. Real estate owners who have fully paid off their properties often look to tap into their equity when they require liquid cash for various expenses. However, rising interest rates mean that borrowing against property assets becomes more expensive than during previous periods of low rates. Financial experts generally advise property owners to carefully evaluate their repayment capabilities and alternative funding sources before committing to new debt in a shifting rate environment. Market conditions fluctuate continuously, influencing the overall cost of borrowing for consumers seeking liquidity from owned assets. The central bank's latest policy update reflects broader macroeconomic strategies aimed at stabilizing the financial sector.

invest.title: ‘It's awful’: How tariffs, soaring fuel costs and higher interest rates are squeezing American companies
invest.excerpt: American companies are facing a challenging economic environment characterised by a combination of tariffs, surging fuel prices and rising interest rates. This triple squeeze is forcing executives to make difficult choices regarding manufacturing, transportation and retail operations. Tariffs have driven up the cost of raw materials and goods, while higher fuel prices increase the expenses associated with making and moving those items. Simultaneously, rising interest rates make it more expensive for businesses to finance necessary inventory and equipment. Middle-market manufacturers and capital-intensive sectors like logistics and commercial real estate are experiencing particularly severe margin pressure. Smaller companies, which typically rely on short-term lending, are passing Federal Reserve rate hikes more directly into their operational costs. Consequently, many businesses are hoarding inventory, cutting less profitable services, or preparing to pass higher expenses on to consumers through increased prices. While some industries such as airlines have successfully maintained profitability by raising fares amidst resilient consumer demand, others are struggling significantly. Certain auto parts manufacturers have halted domestic operations, cancelled plant projects or filed for bankruptcy protection due to these cumulative financial strains. In contrast, large corporations with substantial cash reserves and long-term debt remain better insulated from the immediate impacts of higher borrowing costs.

invest.title: Top Wall Street analysts find these 3 stocks attractive as long-term investments
invest.excerpt: Investors navigating market volatility can look to recommendations from top-performing Wall Street analysts to identify companies with long-term growth potential. Oracle has drawn a buy rating and a $400 price target from Guggenheim analyst John DiFucci following better-than-expected first-quarter results for fiscal 2027. DiFucci highlighted solid growth in cloud infrastructure revenue and expects the company's artificial intelligence training and inferencing opportunities to drive revenue and profit acceleration over the coming years. He also noted that OpenAI's share of Oracle's remaining performance obligations has decreased from 80 percent to about 50 percent as new contracts are signed. Meanwhile, Raymond James analyst Brian Gesuale initiated coverage of Rocket Lab with a buy rating and an $80 price target. Gesuale pointed to the company's upcoming Iridium acquisition, revenue and backlog growth, and a transition from heavy investment to monetization with projected positive free cash flow. In addition, J.P. Morgan analyst Doug Anmuth upgraded Meta Platforms to a buy rating and raised his price target to $820. Anmuth cited Meta's early-stage rollout of frontier models, AI-powered offerings such as the Muse AI agent, and its extensive user base of four billion as key competitive advantages supporting future upside.

invest.title: Williams-Sonoma's stock has soared in a sluggish housing market. Here's how it won over Wall Street
invest.excerpt: Williams-Sonoma has emerged as one of the top-performing retail stocks of the year, with its share price climbing about 23% year to date and outperforming the S&P 1500 Home Furnishings index despite a sluggish housing market in the United States. Chief Executive Officer Laura Alber attributed the success to ongoing improvements in products, service, quality, and storytelling that attract new customers and bring previous ones back. Over a three-year period, the company's shares have risen by more than 200% as management focused on fixing underlying business fundamentals. Savvy operational moves, such as reducing promotional discounts and optimising supply chains for home deliveries, helped drive over 10% expansion in earnings before interest and taxes during difficult market conditions. E-commerce, which accounts for more than two-thirds of sales, has been further bolstered by artificial intelligence tools like a sales assistant named Olive and supply chain cost-reduction applications. Business-to-business sales have also grown, with the company expanding into cruise ships, senior living, and student housing. Pottery Barn, the company's largest brand, recently experienced renewed growth after a post-Covid slump in furniture sales. However, the retailer still faces challenges, notably from tariffs, given that over 80% of its merchandise purchases in 2025 originated from foreign manufacturers. The company previously received a tariff refund of $200 million following a Supreme Court ruling, distributing a portion of the funds to vendors and employees while keeping the refund separate from reported earnings. Analysts point to the company's multi-brand portfolio and omnichannel approach as strong competitive advantages in a fragmented industry.
